       Summary of Responsive Testimony of Mark Garrett

   1                  In his Responsive Testimony, Mr. Garrett addresses OG&E’s request for

   2          preapproval of OG&E’s Electric Service Agreements (“ESAs”) and Capacity Purchase

   3          Agreements (CPAs) with Google, LLC (“Google”) to serve three proposed data center

   4          facilities in Oklahoma. His testimony reviews the specific contractual provisions which

   5          provide protection for existing OG&E customers to ensure that existing customers are not

   6          exposed to stranded costs, cost shifting, or undue financial risk. These provisions include,

   7          among other things:

   8                     1.   Long-term contract commitments;

   9                  2.      Minimum billing demand and energy charges;

  10                  3.      Credit support and guarantees;

  11                  4.      Early termination and capacity-reduction exit fees;

  12                     5.   Google funding of all dedicated transmission and distribution infrastructure

  13                          through Contributions in Aid of Construction (“CI AC”); and

  14                     6.   Provisions recognizing Commission authority to review and address any

  15                          potential adverse rate impact in future rate proceedings through cost-of-

  16                          service adjustments.

  17          The ESAs also provide for tariff-based pricing and potential migration of the Google load

  18          to a future Commission-approved large load tariff, if applicable. Mr. Garrett concludes

  19           that the customer protections included in the Google ESAs are sufficient to protect other

  20           OG&E customers from paying higher costs as a result of adding Google’s load to the

  21           system.



        Summary of Responsive Testimony of Mark E. Garrett                              Page 2 of 4
        Case No. PUD 2026000031
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 116 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/31/2026 - PAGE 3 OF 4




   1                 Mr. Garrett also reviews OG&E’s cost of service studies (“COSS”) which calculate

   2          the costs on OG&E’s system both “with and without” the addition of Google’s load and

   3          resources. In his view, a COSS comparison is a reasonable approach to show that the

   4          addition of Google’s load to OG&E’s system provides a net benefit to the system. He

   5          concludes the COSS comparisons along with the contractual protections appear adequate

   6          to safeguard the interests of existing OG&E customers. He recommends, as a condition

   7          of preapproval, that the Commission require OG&E to present cost of service studies in

   8          future rate cases to demonstrate that Google continues to provide no net detriment to its

   9          system. In the event that a future COSS should demonstrate that Google’s load and

  10          resources are causing an adverse impact on other customers, he recommends that the

  11          Commission adjust Google’s rates at that time, on a prospective basis, to eliminate any

  12          deficiencies going forward that Google may be causing on OG&E’s system.
